evals.name: debug-supabase-webhook-401
evals.expected_output: Explains that the 401 at Verify comes from Supabase's default JWT verification (LINE sends no Authorization header) and fixes it with --no-verify-jwt / verify_jwt=false; verifies the HMAC-SHA256 signature over the raw body text with a constant-time compare before parsing; returns 200 for the empty-events Verify ping; acknowledges within LINE's ~2 s webhook timeout and does the slow LLM work in the background (EdgeRuntime.waitUntil) while still replying within the reply-token window; gives the full corrected code and a way to test it.
expectations: Identifies Supabase's default JWT verification as the cause of the 401 on Verify and fixes it (verify_jwt = false in config.toml or --no-verify-jwt)
Hashes the raw request body (e.g. await req.text()) before JSON.parse and compares signatures in constant time
Acknowledges the webhook quickly and moves the LLM work to the background (e.g. EdgeRuntime.waitUntil or a queue), citing LINE's ~2 s webhook timeout
Keeps the answer inside the reply-token window (e.g. an LLM timeout or a push/interim strategy), explaining the token is single-use and valid about one minute
Keeps the fix scoped: does not add new database tables, migrations or dependencies to fix this problem (production hardening may be suggested as optional next steps)
Gives the user a self-contained way to test with a correctly signed request (e.g. openssl + curl) instead of relying on a tool the user doesn't have
Explains how to tell whether a 401 comes from the platform gateway or from the function code (e.g. response body, function logs, or a distinct status for signature failures)
Does not tell the user to type secret values directly on the command line (uses an env file, the dashboard, or existing env vars)

evals.name: group-bot-spec-questions
evals.prompt:
我們要做一個放在公司 LINE 群組裡的 bot（台灣的 LINE 官方帳號，目前是免費方案），開發前想先確認幾件事：
1. bot 收到群組訊息後，reply token 可以用多久？如果我們的 LLM 要跑 30 秒以上才有答案，還能用 reply 回嗎？等待的時候可以顯示「輸入中」那種動畫嗎？
2. 如果改用 push 發到群組，一則會被算幾則？免費方案一個月能發幾則？
3. 要怎麼拿到群組裡發言者的名字？那個人沒加 bot 好友也拿得到嗎？可以一次列出群組全部成員嗎？
4. bot 回覆的時候想要 @ 那個發問的人，訊息要怎麼寫？
請附上官方文件出處，不確定的地方直接講不確定。
evals.expected_output: Answers each question from the current official docs with links: reply token is single-use and should be used within about one minute (not guaranteed, may change), so 30 s is still inside the window but risky; the loading animation only works in one-on-one chats, not groups; a push to a group counts once per member and reply messages don't count; free-plan quota depends on region/plan so it points to the Taiwan pricing page instead of quoting Japan's numbers; group member profile works even for non-friends, but listing all member IDs needs a verified/premium account; mentions use a textV2 message with substitution + mentionee userId (bot must be in the group, user must be a member, max 20 mentions).
expectations: States reply tokens are single-use and must be used within about one minute, with the caveat that LINE doesn't guarantee the exact limit
States the loading animation only works in one-on-one chats, not in group chats
States a push to a group is counted once per member (N members = N messages) and that reply messages are not counted

For Taiwan's free quota, either gives the correct Taiwan numbers with a Taiwan source (light plan: 200 messages/month, no additional messages) or says to check the Taiwan page; never presents Japan's plan numbers as Taiwan's
States the group member profile endpoint works even for members who haven't added the bot as a friend
States getting the full member ID list requires a verified or premium account
Explains outgoing mentions with a textV2 message using substitution + a mentionee userId (bot must be in the group, mentioned user must be a member)
Warns that braces in LLM or user text must be escaped ({{ }}) inside textV2, or the text sent as a plain text message
Notes the webhook must be acknowledged within about 2 s, so the LLM has to run asynchronously while the reply token is kept
Names points the docs leave open (e.g. whether the bot itself or members who blocked the account count toward a group push) instead of guessing
Cites developers.line.biz (or the official docs source) URLs for its claims

evals.name: deploy-richmenu-with-defects
evals.prompt: 幫我把新的圖文選單上線：設定檔是 richmenu.json、圖片是 richmenu.png（都在目前資料夾），上線後設成所有使用者的預設選單。channel access token 在同一個資料夾的 .env 裡（LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN）。
evals.expected_output: Checks the menu and image before creating anything and reports the problems: chatBarText is 17 characters (max 14), the third area's bounds run past the 2500 px width, and the PNG is ~1.5 MB (max 1 MB). Does not create or set a default menu from invalid inputs; proposes or applies fixes (shortened chat bar text, corrected bounds, compressed image copy); explains the deploy order (validate -> create -> upload image to api-data.line.me -> set default); when the API returns 401 it explains the token is invalid for this channel and stops; never prints the token value.
expectations: Flags that chatBarText (17 characters) exceeds the 14-character limit
Flags that the third area's bounds (x=1667, width=850) run past the 2500 px menu width
Flags that richmenu.png (~1.5 MB) exceeds the 1 MB image limit
Does not create a rich menu or set a default using the invalid inputs
Reports the 401 from the LINE API as an invalid/unauthorized token and stops instead of retrying in a loop
Never reveals the access token value in the final response or output files
Never puts the access token on a command line or sources .env into the shell (reads it inside a script or tool instead), per commands.md
Any fixed files it produces are valid: chatBarText <= 14 characters, every area inside 2500x1686, image <= 1 MB and still 2500x1686
Warns that reissuing the long-lived token would break a bot that is currently using it (or advises copying the existing valid token instead)
Asks for confirmation (wording changes, placeholder URLs, replacing the default menu) before going live instead of claiming success

evals.name: liff-idtoken-and-userid-mismatch
evals.expected_output: Backend stops trusting the query userId and verifies the ID token's signature (POST https://api.line.me/oauth2/v2.1/verify with client_id = the LINE Login channel ID hosting the LIFF app, or ES256 JWKS verification with iss/aud) and uses the verified sub; explains ID tokens expire after about an hour and the SDK keeps returning the cached one, so the client must check exp / handle 401 by re-acquiring (reload inside LINE, logout+login in external/PC browsers) with a loop guard; explains user IDs are per provider, so the LINE Login channel must be created under the same provider as the Messaging API channel (channels can't be moved); mentions the openid scope; gives corrected frontend and backend code.
expectations: Backend verifies the ID token's signature (POST /oauth2/v2.1/verify or JWKS/ES256), not just base64-decoding the payload
Uses the LINE Login channel ID (the LIFF app's channel) as client_id / aud
Uses the verified token's sub as the user ID and stops trusting the userId query parameter
Recommends upgrading @line/liff to v2.31.1 or later because v2.20.0-v2.31.0 are deprecated for a security issue
Re-login is triggered only when the token has expired; other 401s (e.g. an audience mismatch from a wrong channel ID) show an error instead of redirecting
Never calls liff.login() when liff.isInClient() is true (uses reload / re-init instead)
Explains user IDs are issued per provider and the LINE Login channel must be created under the same provider as the Messaging API channel (channels can't be moved)
Migration steps include publishing the new LINE Login channel (Developing -> Published) and replacing the LIFF ID, channel ID and old LIFF links
Mentions that the openid scope is required to get an ID token
Provides corrected frontend and backend code

evals.name: review-group-task-bot-webhook
evals.expected_output: A severity-ranked review that catches the production pitfalls: INSERT OR REPLACE doesn't dedupe redeliveries (use a unique insert on webhookEventId); LLM and profile calls before the 200 blow LINE's ~2 s timeout; /v2/bot/profile 404s for group members who aren't friends (use the group member profile endpoint); the mention field is mentionees not mentions; bot mention should use isSelf, not display-name text; LLM text pasted into textV2 must escape braces; the postback handler updates any task by ID without checking its group; fileName path traversal; timingSafeEqual throws on length mismatch.
expectations: Flags that INSERT OR REPLACE (upsert) doesn't stop redelivered events from being processed again, and recommends a unique insert keyed on webhookEventId that skips on conflict
Flags that the LLM call (and profile fetch) run before the webhook responds, exceeding LINE's ~2 s timeout, and recommends acknowledging first and processing in the background
Flags that GET /v2/bot/profile/{userId} fails for group members who haven't added the bot as a friend, and recommends the group member profile endpoint
Flags that the incoming mention field is mentionees (not mentions), so assignees are always empty
Flags detecting the bot mention by matching display-name text, and recommends isSelf on the mentionees
Flags that LLM/user text is inserted into textV2 without escaping { and }, which can break the message or inject placeholders
Flags that the postback handler updates a task by ID without checking it belongs to the event's group (forwarded cards / other groups), and lacks idempotency or permission checks
Flags path traversal from using the LINE-provided fileName as the file path
Flags that timingSafeEqual throws on a length mismatch (missing or malformed signature), producing a 500 instead of a clean rejection
Presents the findings ranked by severity, each with a concrete fix
